title: Decorative elements must not be focusable
summary: An element with role="presentation" or "none" also has tabindex or a global ARIA attribute, so the role may be ignored. Remove the extra.
problem: An element has role="presentation" or role="none", which tells assistive technology to ignore its meaning. It also has a focusable tabindex or a global ARIA attribute, which makes browsers keep the element meaningful and ignore the role instead.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear a decorative element that was meant to be silent, and keyboard users can tab to something that does nothing.
steps: Find the element in the scan result and the tabindex or ARIA attribute that conflicts with its presentation role.
If the element is truly decorative, remove tabindex and any aria-* attributes from it.
For a decorative image, use an empty alt (alt="") instead of a role, which is shorter and widely supported.
If the element should be interactive or announced, remove the presentation role and give it a proper role and name.
whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice, not a WCAG failure. When the role is silently dropped, people hear and tab to clutter that was meant to be invisible to them.
howToCheck: Tab through the page. Decorative elements must never receive focus. In the accessibility inspector, the element should show as ignored or presentational.
